U-APS Scheduler CLI

Usage:
  uaps <input> <output> [--rule <rule>]        Run scheduler with simple rule
  uaps <input> <output> [--strategy <preset>]  Run with multi-layer strategy
  uaps simulate <input>                        Interactive simulation
  uaps simulate <input> --script <changes.json> --output <out.xlsx>
                                               Batch simulation
  uaps update                                  Update CLI and native library
  uaps version                                 Show version
  uaps help                                    Show this help
  uaps rules                                   List available dispatching rules

Dispatching Rules (--rule/-r):
  Time-based:  SPT (Shortest Processing Time), LPT (Longest Processing Time)
               LWKR (Least Work Remaining), MWKR (Most Work Remaining)
  Due date:    EDD (Earliest Due Date), MST (Minimum Slack Time)
               CR (Critical Ratio), S/RO (Slack per Remaining Operations)
  Queue/Load:  FIFO (First In First Out), WINQ (Work In Next Queue)
               LPUL (Least Planned Utilization Level)
  Priority:    PRIORITY (Job priority field)

Multi-Layer Strategies (--strategy/-S):
  DUE_DATE_FOCUSED  EDD primary, SPT tie-breaker
  THROUGHPUT        SPT only for maximum throughput
  BALANCED          Critical Ratio with FIFO tie-breaker
  URGENCY           Priority-based with EDD secondary
  LOAD_BALANCING    LPUL with WINQ for load distribution
  FAIR              Simple FIFO for fair queuing
  ADAPTIVE          Dynamic rule switching based on conditions

Supported formats:
  - Excel: .xlsx
  - JSON:  .json
  - TSV:   .tsv

Examples:
  uaps input.xlsx output.xlsx
  uaps input.xlsx output.xlsx --rule EDD
  uaps input.xlsx output.xlsx --rule SPT --tie-breaker FIFO
  uaps input.xlsx output.xlsx --strategy BALANCED
  uaps input.xlsx output.xlsx --strategy ADAPTIVE
  uaps simulate input.xlsx
  uaps simulate input.xlsx --script changes.json --output result.xlsx
  uaps update
  uaps rules

result.stdout:
=== Available Dispatching Rules ===

Time-based Rules:
  SPT   - Shortest Processing Time
          Prioritize jobs with shortest processing time first
          Best for: Maximizing throughput, reducing flow time

  LPT   - Longest Processing Time
          Prioritize jobs with longest processing time first
          Best for: Balancing machine loads

  LWKR  - Least Work Remaining
          Prioritize jobs with least remaining work
          Best for: Getting jobs completed faster

  MWKR  - Most Work Remaining
          Prioritize jobs with most remaining work
          Best for: Starting complex jobs early

  WSPT  - Weighted Shortest Processing Time
          Prioritize by weight/processing time ratio
          Best for: Minimizing weighted completion time

Due Date Rules:
  EDD   - Earliest Due Date
          Prioritize jobs with earliest due dates
          Best for: Minimizing maximum lateness

  MST   - Minimum Slack Time
          Prioritize jobs with least buffer time
          Best for: Meeting tight deadlines

  CR    - Critical Ratio
          Prioritize based on (time to due) / (remaining work)
          Best for: Balancing due dates with work remaining

  S/RO  - Slack per Remaining Operations
          Prioritize by slack divided by operations left
          Best for: Complex jobs with multiple operations

  ATC   - Apparent Tardiness Cost
          Combines SPT with due date urgency (exp decay)
          Best for: Minimizing weighted tardiness

Queue/Load Rules:
  FIFO  - First In First Out
          Process jobs in arrival order
          Best for: Fair scheduling, simple cases

  WINQ  - Work In Next Queue
          Prefer jobs heading to less loaded resources
          Best for: Reducing downstream bottlenecks

  LPUL  - Least Planned Utilization Level
          Use resources with lowest planned utilization
          Best for: Balancing resource loads

Priority-based:
  PRIORITY - Job Priority Field
             Use the priority field from job data
             Best for: Business priority-dri
[truncated]
